title: Capability Attribution API + Pinning Hints for Model Onboarding
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Add a conservative, forward-compatible API that exposes an attribution-style capability surface for onboarded models and returns recommended version-pinning hints and lightweight performance profiles. This ticket proposes a new endpoint /v2/models/{model_id}/capability-attribution that complements the existing model manifest endpoints without breaking clients that depend on manifest v1. The endpoint will provide: 1) capability descriptors (features supported such as streaming, function-calling, structured-output), 2) per-capability confidence and provenance (how the capability was detected: static manifest, perf tests, telemetry), 3) compact performance profiles scoped to workload classes (chat, single-turn, embeddings) with p50/p95 latencies, estimated tokens/ms, and suggested batching and quantization knobs, and 4) pinning hints (a small list of model-version candidates and why a customer might pin to them: latency-stable, cost-efficient, high-quality). The API contract emphasizes human-readable strings for feature descriptions and numeric fields for performance metrics; all fields are optional to allow incremental onboarding. Backwards compatibility: clients that do not call /v2 are unaffected. Migration: onboarding workflow will, by default, populate capability-attribution from model-provided metadata and telemetry-derived signals; PMs can opt models in gradually.
acceptance_criteria: New endpoint /v2/models/{model_id}/capability-attribution returns 200 and a JSON body for onboarded models
Fields include: capabilities (list), performance_profiles (list), pinning_hints (list), schema_version string
Each capability entry contains name, confidence (0-1), detected_by (string), and examples (optional)
Performance profile entries include workload_class, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_ms_est, suggested_batch_size, kv_cache_bytes_hint
Pinning hints include version, rationale, suggested_fallbacks, and risk_notes
Unit and integration tests for schema validation and graceful handling when telemetry is absent
API docs and example responses added to developer docs and Console UI wiring stories created
Security review completed and no PII or customer data is surfaced by default

comments: 2026-03-03: Initial spec posted in #model-onboarding. Primary ask: expose machine-readable hints that let product teams safely pin and route to model versions.
2026-03-05: Engineering review - request to keep response size small for heavy listing calls; agreed to cap 'examples' length and provide links to detailed manifests.
2026-03-06: PM feedback - prefer explicit workload_class enum (chat|single_turn|embed|rerank) to avoid downstream mapping ambiguity.
2026-03-08: Design review - Console will show only top-2 pinning_hints and a tooltip for rationale to avoid UI noise.
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff - initial threat model reviewed, flagged telemetry provenance header to avoid accidental customer data exposure.
2026-03-10: Code PR opened for model-catalog read-side translation and unit tests; awaiting load test results before merge.
Blocker: telemetry pipeline for low-volume models currently omits tokens_per_ms estimates; fallback to conservative defaults planned.
notes: Trade-offs: embedding detailed kernel-level perf metrics increases fidelity but also the size of the payload; we prefer a compact summary plus a link to an extended performance artifact stored in S3.
Decision: introduce schema_version and reserve 'capability_flags' for boolean quick-checks; detailed descriptors go under 'capabilities'.
Affinity scoring: simple 0-100 integer score per runtime will be provided initially; future work to normalize across hardware (A100 vs H100) is tracked separately.
Rollback plan: if instrumentation causes load, the endpoint can be routed through a rate-limited facade and default to model manifest values.
Compatibility: We avoided changing existing /manifests endpoints to reduce risk to downstream systems that consume manifest v1.
